data.title: Worldline restricted outflows, boosted inflows to lift cash flow before 2023 stock price crash - FT
data.description:
Worldline (WWLNF) (WRDLY) restricted outflows and boosted inflows before its financial result announcements in the years leading up to the 2023 share price crash, the Financial Times reported, citing documents and three people familiar with the company.

The company delayed payments to suppliers and sought cash advances from customers before half-yearly reporting dates, at least from 2021 to 2023, to lift its disclosed cash flow higher, according to the report published on Friday.

The French digital payments firm's share prices plunged in the fourth quarter of 2023, resulting in takeover speculations. Worldline had issued a shock profit warning in October 2023, which sent the stock prices lower. Credit Agricole (CRARF) was also said to be looking at ways to help out the company.

A PwC report published in late 2023 indicated that Worldline's profit-to-cash conversion rate would have been lower in 2021, 2022, and the first part of 2023 on a "fully normalized" basis, according to the FT.

data.title: PHINIA appoints Treasurer Gordon Muir as CFO
data.description:
PHINIA (PHIN) announced Friday the appointment of Gordon Muir as senior vice president and chief financial officer, effective January 1, 2027.

The company noted that Muir succeeds Chris Gropp, current SVP and CFO, who will retire, effective March 31, 2027.

Gropp will support the transition period starting January 1 through March 31, 2027, as Special Advisor, also reporting to Brady Ericson, president and chief executive officer, focusing on a smooth and well-coordinated transition of responsibilities.

The company noted that Gordon joined BorgWarner in 2007 and has been part of PHINIA since its spin-off in 2023. He currently serves as PHINIA's treasurer, with responsibility for treasury and investor relations, and has played a key role in the company's financial strategy and capital markets activities. 

Source: press release

data.title: Procter & Gamble plans to use AI and automation to free up cash
data.description:
Procter & Gamble (PG) is in the spotlight after the consumer products giant unveiled a renewed cost savings program during its Investor Day event on Thursday. Notably, the Cincinnati-based company committed to a total of another $10B in cost savings in four years through FY30, mostly focused on using AI capabilities to accelerate speed of execution to deliver higher consumer usage and solve consumer problems. A 20% to 30% reduction in product supply workforce (including contractors) and increased use of automation will also factor in.

Following the initiatives, Procter & Gamble (PG) plans to reinvest the extra savings in growth while assuming roughly flat headcount and media spending.

During a Q&A session, CFO Andre Schulten reiterated that the main focus is to reinvest in the business to create the volume and scale that leads to higher margins. "We think this is the right approach given the opportunity to tap in more value-conscious consumers who can then uptrade when disposable income improves," noted JPMorgan analyst Andrea Texeira on the update. "We came away confident that PG can count on its strong moats of digital capabilities, supply chain efficiency, and R&D leadership that should continue to reaccelerate the growth to tackle the remaining 21 out of 50 category/country combinations in which P&G needs to improve share," added Texiera. 

JPMorgan kept its Overweight rating on Procter & Gamble (PG) in place.

Shares of Procter & Gamble (PG) moved 1.3% higher in premarket trading to $169.98. The 52-week high is $173.59.

data.title: Nvidia, AMD in focus as GF Securities says talk of server CPU cuts is 'overstated'
data.description:
Despite rumors that tech companies have started to cut orders for server CPUs, GF Securities said supply chain checks show just the opposite.

The Hong Kong-based investment firm said any talk that Meta (META) and Microsoft (MSFT) have cut orders is inaccurate and that Meta has shifted some purchases of x86 to Nvidia's (NVDA) Grace and Vera server options. Additionally, Meta has accelerated general-server deployments for its Muse artificial intelligence agent.

For Microsoft, orders are unchanged, and any noise is simply reflecting original design manufacturer capacity allocations. 

“Agentic workloads now account for ~80% of tokens on OpenRouter (weekly volume up 35x YoY), with GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol and Claude Duet supporting commercial adoption, while Meta Muse gained 11.2mn NA accounts in 7 weeks but saw Day-30 retention fall to 16.4%,” analysts at the firm wrote in a note to clients. “We maintain server CPU TAM of $211bn by 2030 (+47% CAGR), with 2027 unit growth of 29% (general servers +15%, AI-inference CPUs +79%) as agentic AI expands from 25% to 50% of total inference.”

The investment firm reiterated its Buy rating on AMD as it sees the Dr. Lisa Su-led company benefiting from a ramp in its Venice CPUs and continued share gains in x86 processors.

“We expect Venice to drive further share gains for AMD in the coming quarters, even outperforming Intel’s Diamond Rapids (set to launch by late 1Q27), on the back of superior perf-per-watt, large L3 SRAM, and up to 512 threads,” analysts at the firm added. “For now, we forecast Venice CPU shipments of 400k/5.4mn in 2026/2027, respectively.”

The firm also reiterated its Buy rating on Intel due to the company ramping up its Granite Rapids processors.

data.title: MasTec to acquire mechanical contractor Murphy for about $1.25B
data.description:
MasTec (MTZ) on Friday said it will acquire mechanical contractor Murphy for roughly $1.25 billion in cash.

The company said the deal will boost MasTec’s business in mission-critical infrastructure markets, including aviation and defense, pharmaceutical, healthcare, technology, and advanced manufacturing.

“Murphy expands MasTec’s capabilities in some of the fastest-growing and most diverse infrastructure markets in North America. Its highly skilled union craft workforce, supported by established apprenticeship, training and field-leadership programs, provides the labor capacity and execution expertise required to deliver large, complex projects safely and efficiently,” said MasTec’s Chief Executive Officer Jose Mas.

Murphy will serve as a new operating group of MasTec, and Murphy’s financial results are expected to be reflected in the Clean Energy and Infrastructure Segment, MasTec said. Murphy's management team, led by President and Chief Executive Officer Patrick Murphy, will remain in place following the transaction.

MasTec said there is a potential earnout payment based on the cumulative three-year financial performance of Murphy post-closing.

Murphy is projected to generate full calendar year 2026 revenue and an adjusted EBITDA of about $775 million and roughly $140 million, respectively, it added.

Shares of MasTec, which is an infrastructure engineering and construction company, were down over 1% in premarket trading.

data.title: Union Pacific powers past controversy in its bid to merge with Norfolk Southern
data.description:
Union Pacific (UNP) and Norfolk Southern (NSC) filed a response to Canadian Pacific Kansas City's (CPKC) request that the Surface Transportation Board terminate review of the merger application for a transcontinental railroad.

On October 30, rival Class I railroad Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC) seized on the old remarks made by Union Pacific (UNP) CEO Jim Vena on raising rates to certain customers to "teach you a lesson"  to aggressively challenge the merger review process. Union Pacific (UNP) clarified that it "does not retaliate against customers" and insisted a shipper's stance on the merger would never affect its rates or service.

Union Pacific (UNP) and Norfolk Southern (NSC) noted that they remain focused on advancing a transaction that will give U.S. businesses more options to compete in the global marketplace, lower transportation costs, and protect tens-of-thousands of union jobs. The companies said they look forward to the Surface Transportation Board continued evaluation of the proposed combination based on the facts, evidence, and public interest benefits presented in the record. 

Written public comments on the proposed merger closed on November 18, and preliminary comments from the Department of Justice and the Department of Transportation are due on December 3. Union Pacific (UNP) and Norfolk Southern (NSC) must submit their responses to these comments by February 16, 2027, followed by a public STB hearing scheduled to take place after March 29, 2027. Final briefs are due on May 28, 2027, after which the evidentiary record will close. The STB is expected to issue its final decision within 90 days of the record closing, targeting final approval and transaction completion by late summer 2027.

data.title: Equinor says cyberattack against it has been stopped
data.description:
Equinor (EQNR) said Friday that the cyberattack against it has been stopped with no ⁠impact to production ​and no ​indication data had been stolen or altered.

Europe's largest gas ​supplier had detected the attack three days ago but said it was not a virus attack, so there was no chance of it spreading, and that it also did not appear to be specifically targeting the company.

At least two Norwegian energy companies reported a cyberattack or an attempted attack at around the same time this week.

"There is also no indication that the attack has had any negative consequences for employees, partners, or suppliers," Equinor (EQNR) said.
